paragraphs.title: Attempts to Lure and Intimidate Nehemiah

easy.explanation: Sanballat and Geshem sent the invitation to meet Nehemiah.
easy.q: Who sent messengers to Nehemiah saying, “Come, let us meet together”?

easy.explanation: The wall had been built, but the doors had not yet been set up upon the gates.
easy.q: What had Nehemiah not yet set up upon the gates?

easy.explanation: Nehemiah said, “I am doing a great work.”
easy.q: How did Nehemiah describe the work he was doing?

medium.explanation: They sent the invitation four times, and Nehemiah answered them in the same manner.
medium.q: How many times did Sanballat and Geshem send the same invitation before the fifth attempt?

answers: Because he was doing the work
Because he did not know the way
medium.explanation: Nehemiah said he could not come down because he was doing a great work.
medium.q: Why did Nehemiah refuse to come down to meet Sanballat and Geshem?

medium.explanation: To cease means to stop, and Nehemiah would not stop the work to meet them.
medium.q: In the statement “why should the work cease,” what does “cease” mean?

answers: To announce that the wall was finished
challenge.explanation: The report was intended to make Nehemiah afraid and put pressure on him.
challenge.q: What was the purpose of the report that Nehemiah and the Jews planned to rebel?

answers: As a message from the king
As things invented out of Sanballat’s own heart
challenge.explanation: Nehemiah answered that Sanballat was feigning or inventing the accusations out of his own heart.
challenge.q: How did Nehemiah describe the accusations written against him?

challenge.explanation: Nehemiah prayed, “O God, strengthen my hands,” so that he could continue the work.
challenge.q: What did Nehemiah ask God to do at the end of his response?

paragraphs.title: Shemaiah’s Plot and the False Warnings

easy.explanation: Shemaiah advised Nehemiah to hide in the Temple.
easy.q: Who urged Nehemiah to meet in the house of God within the Temple?

easy.explanation: Shemaiah said that men would come to slay Nehemiah, even in the night.
easy.q: What danger did Shemaiah claim was coming upon Nehemiah?

answers: He asked to wait until morning
He said, “I will not go in”
easy.explanation: Nehemiah refused to enter the Temple and said, “I will not go in.”
easy.q: What was Nehemiah’s response to Shemaiah’s proposal?

answers: He was not permitted to enter it
The Temple was too far away
The Temple doors were already shut
medium.explanation: Nehemiah understood that entering the Temple in this way was not lawful for him.
medium.q: Why did Nehemiah refuse to flee into the Temple?

medium.explanation: “Shut up” means that Shemaiah was confined or kept inside.
medium.q: What does “shut up” mean in the description of Shemaiah?

answers: To make him afraid and sin
To protect the people of Judah
medium.explanation: Nehemiah realized that the proposal was intended to frighten him, make him sin, and provide an evil report against him.
medium.q: What did Nehemiah perceive was the purpose of Shemaiah’s proposal?

answers: That the people had sent him
That God had not sent him
challenge.explanation: Nehemiah perceived that God had not sent Shemaiah.
challenge.q: What did Nehemiah perceive about the source of Shemaiah’s prophecy?

challenge.explanation: Nehemiah said that Tobiah and Sanballat had hired Shemaiah.
challenge.q: Who had hired Shemaiah according to Nehemiah?

answers: Noadiah the prophetess and the rest of the prophets
All the workers on the wall
challenge.explanation: Nehemiah asked God to remember Noadiah the prophetess and the rest of the prophets who tried to frighten him.
challenge.q: Who else did Nehemiah mention among those who tried to put him in fear?

paragraphs.title: Completion of the Wall and Recognition of Divine Assistance

answers: The twenty and fifth day of Elul
The twenty and fifth day of Tishri
easy.explanation: The wall was finished on the twenty and fifth day of the month Elul.
easy.q: On what day was the wall finished?

easy.explanation: The wall was completed in fifty and two days.
easy.q: How long did the work take?

answers: They were much cast down in their own eyes
easy.explanation: They were much cast down in their own eyes because the work had succeeded.
easy.q: How did the enemies and surrounding heathen react when they heard of the completion?

answers: That it was wrought of God
That the wall was still broken
medium.explanation: They perceived that the work was wrought of their God.
medium.q: What did the enemies and surrounding peoples perceive about the work?

answers: They succeeded in stopping the work
They did not stop the work
They caused Nehemiah to leave Jerusalem
medium.explanation: The wall was completed, showing that the threats did not stop the work.
medium.q: What does the completion of the wall show about the attempts to frighten Nehemiah?

answers: They saw that the work had succeeded
medium.explanation: The success of the work caused them to feel humbled and defeated.
medium.q: Why were the enemies cast down in their own eyes?

answers: The work was recognized as wrought of God
The work was described as an accident
The work was credited to the enemies
challenge.explanation: The surrounding peoples perceived that the work was wrought of God.
challenge.q: What connection do the verses make between the successful work and faith in God?

answers: It was finished in fifty and two days
It was finished before the work began
challenge.explanation: The verse specifically states that the wall was finished in fifty and two days.
challenge.q: Which detail gives the exact duration of the construction?

answers: They recognized divine help in the work
They invited Nehemiah to meet them
They continued the same false report
challenge.explanation: Their recognition that God had accomplished the work gave the victory spiritual significance.
challenge.q: How does the reaction of the surrounding peoples strengthen the meaning of the victory?

paragraphs.title: Tobiah’s Connections and Continuing Internal Tension

easy.explanation: The nobles of Judah sent many letters unto Tobiah.
easy.q: To whom did the nobles of Judah send many letters?

answers: He was the son-in-law of Shechaniah
He was the son of Nehemiah
He was a prophet in Jerusalem
easy.explanation: Many in Judah were sworn to Tobiah because he was the son-in-law of Shechaniah.
easy.q: What family connection did Tobiah have in Judah?

answers: To invite him into the Temple
easy.explanation: Tobiah sent letters to put Nehemiah in fear.
easy.q: Why did Tobiah send letters to Nehemiah?

answers: Because of his marriage connection with Shechaniah’s family
Because he had built the wall
Because he was a prophet in Jerusalem
medium.explanation: Many were bound to Tobiah because he was the son-in-law of Shechaniah.
medium.q: Why were many in Judah sworn unto Tobiah?

answers: They reported information between the sides
They wrote only about the wall
medium.explanation: The nobles reported Tobiah’s good deeds to Nehemiah and uttered Nehemiah’s words to Tobiah.
medium.q: What did the nobles and Tobiah do with information about Nehemiah?

medium.explanation: The phrase means to cause Nehemiah to be afraid.
medium.q: In the phrase “to put me in fear,” what does “put me in fear” mean?

answers: The tension did not end with the completion of the wall
challenge.explanation: The letters show that opposition and political tension continued after the wall was completed.
challenge.q: What does the continued correspondence after the wall was finished show?

answers: They caused the gates to be closed
challenge.explanation: Family connections caused many people in Judah to be sworn or loyal to Tobiah.
challenge.q: How did marriage connections affect the internal situation in Judah?

answers: An invitation to work with the builders
challenge.explanation: Tobiah used letters to put Nehemiah in fear.
challenge.q: What means of pressure did Tobiah use against Nehemiah?
